Figure 2: Intuitive illustration of SpecSteer. Standard speculative verification (A) may wrongly reject valid private entities (e.g., “Gino’s”) because the Generalist assigns them low absolute probability in the absence of private context. In contrast, SpecSteer (B) first performs ratio-based verification, normalizing the Generalist’s score by a generic baseline (PSLM− ) to filter out surprise caused by missing private knowledge. Draft tokens that pass the ratio test are accepted directly, while failed cases are handled by steering recovery, which re-injects the Specialist’s personalized signal to recover the intended continuation without exposing private data.
